title: Scholastic ‘adoration’: whole cult, or the special bodily signs (prostration, genuflection) Thomas ranks first among exterior latria acts
source_text: X. Obiter autem hic notandum apud Doctores Scholasticos adorationis vocem alio adhuc respectu, modo strictiorem, modo vero ampliorem significatum habere. Nam latiore sensu adoratio comprehendit totum cultum qui sive Deo, sive Sanctis exhibendus est, sed quandoque strictius sumitur pro specialibus quibusdam actibus cultus sive Deo, sive Sanctis debiti. Unde est quod Scholastici quandoque inter actus adorationis numerant sacrificium, collationem & susceptionem Sacramentorum, petitionem gratiae & veniae, percussionem pectoris, templorum constructionem, institutionem festorum, vota denique & juramenta: quandoque volunt adorationem esse specialem religionis actum a Sacrificio, ab oratione, voto, juramento, &c. distinctum. Ut videre est apud Thomam Aquinatem in secunda secundae quaestione 84. Ubi adorationi primum locum inter actus exteriores latriae assignat, & adorationis nomine intelligit eam per quam aliquis corpus suum ad Deum venerandum exhibet. Adeoque Adoratio stricto illo sensu sumpta consistit in externis submissionis signis ex interno affectu ei quem colere volumus exhibitis. Qualia signa sunt prostratio corporis, genuflexio, aut aliquid simile.
pass_a_gloss: But here it is to be noted in passing among the Scholastic Doctors that the voice of adoration has, under yet another respect, now a stricter, now a more ample signification. For in the broader sense adoration comprehends the whole cult which is to be exhibited either to God or to the Saints, but sometimes it is taken more strictly for certain special acts of cult owed either to God or to the Saints. Whence it is that the Scholastics sometimes number among the acts of adoration sacrifice, the conferring and receiving of the Sacraments, petition of grace and pardon, beating of the breast, construction of temples, institution of feasts, finally vows and oaths: sometimes they will adoration to be a special act of religion distinct from Sacrifice, from prayer, vow, oath, etc. As is to be seen in Thomas Aquinas in the second of the second, question 84. Where he assigns to adoration the first place among the exterior acts of latria, and by the name of adoration understands that by which someone exhibits his body for the venerating of God. And so Adoration taken in that strict sense consists in exterior signs of submission exhibited from an interior affection to him whom we will to cultivate. Such signs are prostration of the body, genuflection, or something similar.
pass_b_english: Scholastics stretch ‘adoration’ from the whole cult-package to a special exterior act.
Thomas (2a2ae q.84) puts bodily exhibition—prostration, genuflection—first among exterior latria acts.
Strict adoration = outward submission-signs springing from inward affection.

choices.why: Thomas locus for adoration among latria acts.
